newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: House of rebel Tajik colonel comes under fire.
newsitem.headline: House of rebel Tajik colonel comes under fire.

text.p: The house of rebel Tajik Colonel Makhmud Khudoyberdyev came under fire from automatic weapons on Thursday, casting doubts over an agreement that halted days of fighting in Tajikistan.

Reuter correspondents in Kurgan Tyube, Khudoyberdyev's stronghold, heard his forces respond with an artillery gun and said he had blamed the attack on government troops. The Tajik government said earlier that the rebel colonel had agreed to withdraw his forces to barracks after peace talks.

Speaking to Reuters minutes before the attack on Kurgan Tyube, 110 km (70 miles) south of the capital Dushanbe, Khodoyberdyev said the government was not fulfilling its part of the agreement and had failed to withdraw its armour to base.
"They do not want to withdraw. I think the president is just powerless now. It is not his fault, it is the fault of certain commanders who want to take control of Kurgan Tyube," he said.

He later blamed the attack on government troops, some of which are stationed 12 km (eight miles) from his stronghold. Asked what would happen if the government did not withdraw its troops, Khudoyberdyev said: "Honestly, I think it could only be war."
He added he still considered himself to be in charge of the elite brigade he has commanded until now, despite an order by President Imomali Rakhmonov removing him from the post.
